title: Gospel of Thomas, sayings 110-114 and subscript title (Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 51)
source: Nag Hammadi Codex II page photographs (Claremont Colleges Digital Library, Nag Hammadi Archive) + Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition by Paul Dilley (CC BY 4.0) + English by Mark M. Mattison (public domain)
description: Gospel of Thomas, sayings 110-114 and subscript title, in the Coptic of Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 51, with each saying linked to the photograph of the papyrus page and an English translation.
introduction:
The Gospel of Thomas is a collection of 114 sayings attributed to Jesus, introduced as the hidden sayings written down by Didymos Judas Thomas. The only complete copy is the second tractate of Nag Hammadi Codex II, a papyrus book in Coptic copied in the 4th century and found near Nag Hammadi in Upper Egypt in 1945; it is now in the Coptic Museum, Cairo (inv. 10544). Greek fragments of the work survive in three Oxyrhynchus papyri (P. Oxy. 1, 654 and 655), which are not shown here.

This entry covers the sayings 110-114 and subscript title, which begin on codex page 51. The Coptic is given line by line; the small numbers are codex page and line (for example 33.5), so each line can be found on the photograph. Page and line breaks follow the Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition by Paul Dilley, which he made from the photographs of The Facsimile Edition of the Nag Hammadi Codices, the negatives shown here.

Photograph: Codex II page 51, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 63, CCDL nha 2842; Nag Hammadi Archive of the Institute for Antiquity and Christianity, Claremont Colleges Digital Library. Checked on the photograph: page 51 line 1 begins 'ⲧⲥⲱϣⲉ ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲁⲩ ⲁϥⲧⲁ̣ⲁ̣[ⲥ ⲉⲃⲟ]ⲗ̣ ̣ⲁ̣ⲩ̣ⲱ̣ ̣ⲡ̣[ⲉⲛ]ⲧ' and line 28 reads 'ⲡⲕⲁⲧⲁ ⲑⲱⲙⲁⲥ' (the last saying ends on line 26; the title stands on lines 27-28 between ornamental bands, and the Gospel of Philip begins below).
translator_notes: Coptic: Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition (Paul C. Dilley), version 6.2.0, CC BY 4.0, shown in the manuscript's own spelling with words grouped as bound groups. Editorial signs are the edition's: square brackets mark letters lost in a gap (restored by the editor, or dots for the number of lost letters), a dot under a letter marks an uncertain reading, round brackets write out a letter abbreviated by a stroke at a line end, angle brackets mark letters added by the editor, curly brackets letters the editor removes, double square brackets letters erased by the scribe.

The small numbers in the Coptic are codex page and line (page.line) as marked in the edition. Where a word is divided between two lines on the papyrus, the edition sometimes keeps the word whole on one line, so a line can begin a few letters earlier or later on the photograph (for example 39.33-34, and the page change inside saying 13).

English: Mark M. Mattison, The Gospel of Thomas (public domain). Mattison's symbols: [ ] gap in the text, ( ) editorial insertion, / \ editorial correction of a scribal error. The saying headings are his.
Saying 114: Mattison discusses the rendering 'manly' in his book The Gospel of Thomas: A New Translation for Spiritual Seekers (2015), pp. 25-26.

translation.text: Jesus said, "Whoever has found the world and become rich should renounce the world."
translation.scan_note: On page 51 lines 4-5 (Codex II page 51, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 63, CCDL nha 2842). translation.text:
Jesus said, "The heavens and the earth will roll up in front of you, and whoever lives from the Living One won't see death."

Doesn't Jesus say, "Whoever finds themselves, of them the world isn't worthy"?

translation.text:
His disciples said to him, "When will the kingdom come?"

"It won't come by looking for it. They won't say, 'Look over here!' or 'Look over there!' Rather, the Father's kingdom is already spread out over the earth, and people don't see it."

51.26ⲛⲙ̄ⲡⲏⲩⲉ
translation.text:
Simon Peter said to them, "Mary should leave us, because women aren't worthy of life."

Jesus said, "Look, am I to make her a man? So that she may become a living spirit too, she's equal to you men, because every woman who makes herself manly will enter the kingdom of heaven."
